successCriteria.description: Every method declared in `IBalanceRepository` (`findById`, `findByEmployeeAndYear`, `findByEmployeeYearAndPolicy`, `create`, `update`, `deductPendingDays`, `commitDeduction`, `restorePendingDays`) accepts an optional `client?: PoolClient` parameter as its last argument.
When a `client` is passed to any `BalanceRepository` method, the method executes its query using that client (not the shared pool), enabling the caller to orchestrate multi-step transactions.
When no `client` is passed, every `BalanceRepository` method continues to use the shared `pool` for single-step operations — backward compatibility is preserved.

`BalanceRepository.create` detects duplicate `(employee_id, policy_id, fiscal_year)` insertions and throws a typed domain error (e.g. `DuplicateBalanceError`) instead of letting a raw PostgreSQL unique-violation error propagate.

constraints: The `client` parameter must be typed as `PoolClient` from the `pg` package (the same type already used by `src/shared/db/connection.ts`).

Duplicate detection in `create` must use either `ON CONFLICT (employee_id, policy_id, fiscal_year) DO NOTHING` with a follow-up SELECT, or catch the unique-violation error code (`23505`) from PostgreSQL — no pre-query check-then-insert pattern that would create a TOCTOU race.
The `IBalanceRepository` interface change is additive — all existing method signatures remain callable without a `client` argument. No existing call site in `BalanceService` or tests may break.
outOfScope: Adding `client?: PoolClient` to any repository interface other than `IBalanceRepository` (e.g. `IEmployeeRepository`, `IPolicyRepository`, `IAuditRepository`, `INotificationRepository`) — those are deferred to later phases.

Modifying `BalanceService` to pass a `client` to repository methods or to orchestrate transactions — this phase only adds the capability to the repository interface and implementation; the service continues to call without a client.

ambiguities.description: The name of the duplicate-balance error type is not specified in PLAN.md or the reconciled architecture. The code agent must choose a name (e.g. `DuplicateBalanceError`) consistent with the existing pattern: `DuplicateLeaveTypeError` in policy, `DuplicateEmployeeNumberError` in employee.

entityInvariants.invariant: A `LeaveBalance` is uniquely identified by the composite `(employeeId, policyId, fiscalYear)`. No two balance records may exist with the same triple. The repository `create` method must enforce this by rejecting duplicates with a typed domain error.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Throws a typed domain error (e.g. `DuplicateBalanceError`) when a balance already exists for the same `(employeeId, policyId, fiscalYear)` triple. Must not leak raw PostgreSQL error codes to callers.

Every method accepts an optional trailing `client?: PoolClient` parameter. When provided, the query executes on that client; when omitted, the method uses the shared pool. The `client` parameter is always the last argument.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The `client?: PoolClient` parameter pattern must match the transaction contract defined in `.gestalt/architecture/reconciled.json`: "Repository methods that participate in multi-step writes accept an optional `client: PoolClient` parameter. When omitted, the method acquires its own connection from the shared pool for single-step operations."

The `IBalanceRepository` interface must remain consistent with the existing `BalanceService` usage — all service methods (`getOrCreateBalance`, `reserveDays`, `commitDays`, `restoreDays`, `hasSufficientBalance`, `getBalancesForEmployee`, `getById`) call repository methods without a `client` argument today and must continue to compile and pass tests.
The `BalanceRepository` implementation must continue to use the shared `pool` from `src/shared/db/connection.ts` as its default connection source when no `client` is provided.

The duplicate-handling pattern in `create` must be consistent with the existing `PolicyRepository.create` approach (which throws `DuplicateLeaveTypeError`), but must use a race-condition-free mechanism (`ON CONFLICT` or error-code catch) rather than a pre-check-then-insert pattern.
